newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND TO SELL 15 PCT OF PAPER FIRM IN APRIL OFFER.
newsitem.headline: POLAND TO SELL 15 PCT OF PAPER FIRM IN APRIL OFFER.

text.p: Poland will sell 7.5 million shares or 15 percent of paper firm Celuloza Swiecie SA in an April public offering and seek an investor for another 65 percent of shares, the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) said.
Karol Milkowski, a treasury ministry official, told a news conference on Thursday that the strategic investor would also likely be chosen in April.
"The treasury ministry is considering offers and we assume that by April 8 we will be able to sign an agreement with a strategic investor," Karol Milkowski said.
The KPW said in its Thursday statement it had cleared all Celuloza Swiecie's 50 million shares, of which another 15 percent would be earmarked for employees.

Five percent of the firm, whose full name is Zaklady Celulozy i Papieru w Swieciu Celuloza SA and which has a 25 percent of the domestic market, would go to restitution claims for property confiscated under communism.
The statement said investors could subscribe for up to 2.5 million shares from April 14 to April 18 and that the shares would be allotted at a special bourse session on April 22.
It said the shares would be offered at a minimum price to be announced later.
In 1995, the last year for which full results are available, Celuloza Swiecie made a net profit of 110.3 million zlotys on sales of 760.1 million zlotys.
In the first half of 1996 it netted 48.9 million zlotys on sales of 365.4 million zlotys.
The firm has said it expects to net 80 million zlotys on sales of 714 million zloty sales in 1996.
The company would become one of the largest on the Warsaw bourse. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
